propositions.text: The claimants are a family from Egypt seeking refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).
propositions.quote: These are the reasons for the decision in the claims of Mr. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ("the claimant"), Ms. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ("the female claimant"), and XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ("the minor claimants"), who claim to be citizens of Egypt and are seeking refugee protection pursuant to section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The court states the claimants are an Egyptian family seeking refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).

propositions.text: The claimants' claims were joined under Rule 55, with the principal claimant as representative for the minors.
propositions.quote: As the claimants are a married couple and their two sons, aged six and eight years respectively, their claims were joined pursuant to Rule 55 of the Refugee Protection Division Rules, with the principal claimant assigned as the designated representative for the two minors.

propositions.text: All claimants rely on the allegations in the claimant's Basis of Claim, file TB8-29231.
propositions.quote: All four claimants rely on the allegations as stated in the claimant's Basis of Claim, RPD file number TB8-29231.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains the claims were joined under Rule 55 and rely on the claimant's Basis of Claim.

propositions.text: IRPA s.170(f) allows RPD to decide claims without a hearing unless the Minister intervenes timely.
propositions.quote: Paragraph 170(f) of IRPA provides that the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) may allow a claim for refugee protection without a hearing, unless the Minister has notified the RPD of the Minister's intention to intervene within the time limit set out in the Refugee Protection Division Rules.

propositions.text: IRPA s.162(2) requires proceedings to be informal and quick, respecting fairness and natural justice.
propositions.quote: Further, subsection 162(2) of IRPA directs each Division to deal with all proceedings before it as informally and quickly as the circumstances and the considerations of fairness and natural justice permit.

paragraphs.summary: The court cites IRPA provisions allowing expedited decisions without hearings unless the Minister intervenes, and requiring informal, quick proceedings.

propositions.text: The claimant's case was identified for expedited processing; security screening was received in Dec 2018 and Mar 2019.
propositions.quote: The claimant's case was identified as one that could be processed through the RPD's expedited process for Egyptian claims. Security screening results for the claimant were received by the RPD on December 18, 2018, and for the female claimant on March 13, 2019.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the claimant's case was selected for expedited processing with security screening received in late 2018 and early 2019.

propositions.text: The claimant signed a Certificate of Readiness for expedited process on April 12, 2019.
propositions.quote: The RPD received the claimant's signed Certificate of Readiness for the expedited process on April 12, 2019.

propositions.text: The panel finds the case meets criteria for expedited determination and decides without a hearing.
propositions.quote: Having carefully considered the evidence in this case, the panel finds that it meets the criteria for expedited determination. This case has therefore been decided without a hearing, according to the Instructions governing the streaming of less complex claims at the Refugee Protection Division.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the case meets expedited criteria and decides it without a hearing based on the claimant's readiness certificate.

propositions.text: The claimants are Coptic Christians from Egypt fearing harm from Muslim extremists, with worsening conditions after 2011 revolution.
propositions.quote: According to the allegations outlined in the narrative to the Basis of Claim, the claimants are Coptic Christian residents of XXXX who fear harm at the hands of Muslim extremists in Egypt. While the family had in the past experienced discrimination on the basis of religious identity in Egypt, their circumstances changed for the worse following the events of the 2011 revolution.

propositions.text: The claimants applied for Canadian permanent residence in 2011 but were informed it was unsuccessful.
propositions.quote: The same year, the claimant and his spouse applied for permanent residence in Canada, hoping to leave Egypt with their newborn son. While they never received a formal rejection, their consultant informed them that the application was unsuccessful.

propositions.text: The claimant opened a business and spouse worked at a XXXX, facing verbal and physical assaults including on way to church.
propositions.quote: After their second son was born, the claimant opened his own XXXX XXXX while his spouse worked as a XXXX at a XXXX XXXX. She faced verbal and physical assaults at work and on her way to church.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker reports the claimants are Coptic Christians fearing Muslim extremists, with worsening conditions post-2011 and prior failed Canadian residence application.

propositions.text: In 2017, the claimant was attacked leaving church; police were called but attackers fled.
propositions.quote: In XXXX 2017, while leaving church with fellow worshippers, the claimant was attacked by a group of extremists who fled when the police were called.

propositions.text: In 2018, Muslim men ordered the claimant to close his business; he was assaulted and threatened when he refused.
propositions.quote: In XXXX 2018, four Muslim men came to the claimant's XXXX XXXX and ordered him to close it. When he refused, he was assaulted and threatened with further harm.

propositions.text: After another assault outside church, the claimants fled Egypt and filed refugee claims in Canada in Nov 2018.
propositions.quote: Following another assault outside their church, the claimants fled Egypt for Canada, filing their claims for refugee protection inland on November 14, 2018.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds the claimant was attacked in 2017 and 2018, leading the family to flee Egypt and file refugee claims in 2018.

propositions.text: The claimants fear persecution by radical Islamists due to religion and allege state protection is unavailable.
propositions.quote: The claimants fear persecution and harm at the hands of radical Islamists and other extremists on the basis of religion in Egypt. They also allege that the Egyptian authorities are unable or unwilling to protect them as Coptic Christians.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker reports the claimants allege fear of persecution by Islamists and lack of state protection in Egypt.

propositions.text: The panel finds the claimants are Convention refugees under IRPA section 96 for stated reasons.
propositions.quote: The panel finds that the claimants are Convention refugees under section 96 of IRPA for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimants are Convention refugees under IRPA section 96.

propositions.text: The claimants' Egyptian nationality is established on balance of probabilities by their passports seized by IRCC.
propositions.quote: The claimants' identities as nationals of Egypt have been established, on a balance of probabilities, by their Arab Republic of Egypt passports that were seized by the referring IRCC office.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimants' Egyptian nationality established by passports seized by IRCC.

propositions.text: The claimants' Coptic Christian identity is established by personal documents including identity cards and church letters.
propositions.quote: The claimants have also established their identities as Coptic Christians by way of their personal documentation, including the following: national identity cards; birth, marriage, and baptism certificates; letters from churches in Egypt and Canada; and photographs depicting the claimants engaged in religious ceremonies and church activities.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimants' Coptic Christian identity established by personal and church documents.

propositions.text: The panel finds the claimants credible on central elements: Christian Copts targeted and assaulted for religion in Egypt.
propositions.quote: The panel has reviewed the claimant's Basis of Claim (BOC), intake forms, and personal documentation disclosed, and has found the claimants to be credible regarding the central elements in this case - namely that they are Christian Copts and have previously been targeted and assaulted on the basis of their religious identity in Egypt.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimants credible on key facts of being Christian Copts targeted and assaulted in Egypt.

propositions.text: The claimants' personal evidence is consistent with country conditions documents, establishing their profile as targeted Christian Egyptians.
propositions.quote: In reviewing the National Documentation Package (NDP) for Egypt, the panel has found the claimants' personal evidence to be consistent with the objective country conditions documents before it. As such, the panel finds that the claimants have established, on a balance of probabilities, their profile as Christian Egyptian citizens who have been targeted by Muslim extremists because of their religion.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimants' evidence consistent with country conditions, establishing their profile as targeted Christian Egyptians.

propositions.text: The refugee test under IRPA section 96 is whether there is a serious possibility of persecution if returned.
propositions.quote: As religion forms a basis for refugee claims, as per section 96 of IRPA, the test is whether there is a serious possibility of persecution should the claimants return to Egypt.

propositions.text: The panel finds the claimants have met the test of serious possibility of persecution based on the evidence.
propositions.quote: The panel finds, based on the evidence before it, that the claimants have met that test.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the refugee test is serious possibility of persecution and finds the claimants meet it.

propositions.text: To succeed under IRPA s.96, claimants must rebut the presumption of state protection.
propositions.quote: In order to establish a claim pursuant to section 96 of the IRPA, the claimant must rebut the presumption of state protection.

propositions.text: The claimants observed police unwillingness to act in religious disputes and believed police would not protect them as Christians.
propositions.quote: The claimants had in the past observed that the police were not willing to act in matters of religious disputes, and came to believe that the police would not protect them, as Christians, in any matters arising from a sectarian conflict between Christian and Muslim residents in Egypt.

paragraphs.summary: The court states claimants must rebut state protection presumption; claimants believe police would not protect them as Christians.

propositions.text: Country documents show ongoing sectarian violence against Copts since ousting of President Morsi.
propositions.quote: The panel has before it country conditions documentation indicating that Copts have complained of ongoing sectarian violence, including targeted kidnappings, armed robberies, and assault since the ousting of former President Morsi.

propositions.text: Authorities have failed to protect Copts adequately, creating a climate of impunity for sectarian violence.
propositions.quote: There are longstanding allegations that the authorities have failed to provide sufficient protection for the Coptic community, and that inadequate police response has created a climate of impunity: Societal violence connected with religion, including terrorist attacks, continued. ... ISIS claimed responsibility for multiple attacks, including suicide bombings at two churches during Palm Sunday services that killed 45 people, the killing of 28 passengers on a bus carrying Christian pilgrims to a desert monastery, and numerous killings of Christians in northern Sinai and elsewhere. Muslims opposed to church construction or renovation, even when legally authorized, continued to commit violence against churches and Christian-owned properties in various locales. Victims of sectarian violence continued to be pressured to drop charges in the spirit of "reconciliation" - a practice which human rights groups and Christians said regularly failed to hold the perpetrators accountable or provide justice to victims and their families. Muslims who openly left Islam were subjected to violence, threats, and abuse. Christians continued to face societal discrimination in their daily lives.

paragraphs.summary: The court cites country documents showing ongoing sectarian violence and inadequate state protection for Copts since Morsi's ousting.

propositions.text: Country documents confirm Christians are targeted by militants and state authorities are slow to act.
propositions.quote: Country documentation confirms that Christians continue to be targeted by Islamic militants, attacks against Copts take place throughout Egypt, and state authorities are slow to act: "Amnesty International reports that religious minorities, 'including Coptic Christians..., continued to face discriminatory restrictions in law and practice and inadequate protection from violence'."

paragraphs.summary: The court notes country documents confirm Christians face militant attacks and inadequate state protection in Egypt.

propositions.text: The objective evidence supports claimants' allegations and shows clear, convincing evidence of state's inability to protect them.
propositions.quote: The panel finds that the objective documentary evidence before it supports the claimants' allegations, and that they have provided clear and convincing evidence of the state's inability to protect them as Coptic Christians should they return to Egypt.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds objective evidence supports claimants' allegations and shows state's inability to protect them.

propositions.text: There is a serious possibility claimants face persecution by Muslim extremists and lack state protection if returned to Egypt.
propositions.quote: Given the documentary evidence before the panel, both personal and objective, the panel finds that there is a serious possibility that the claimants could face persecution and harm at the hands of Muslim extremists and radical Islamists should they return to Egypt, and that state protection would not reasonably be forthcoming to them as Christians anywhere in the country.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds a serious possibility of persecution and lack of state protection for claimants if returned to Egypt.

propositions.text: The panel determines claimants have established serious possibility of persecution on a Convention ground under IRPA section 96 if returned to Egypt.
propositions.quote: Based on the foregoing analysis, the panel has determined that the claimants have established that there is a serious possibility of persecution on a Convention ground as per section 96 of IRPA if they were to return to Egypt.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimants have established serious possibility of persecution under IRPA section 96 if returned to Egypt.

propositions.text: The panel finds the claimants are Convention refugees and accepts the claims.
propositions.quote: The panel therefore finds that the claimants are Convention refugees and accepts the claims.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimants are Convention refugees and accepts the claims, as stated by the court.
